Garden Stops for Motorcycle Tourers

Not every touring stop needs to be a mountain pass or a dramatic viewpoint. Britain's botanical gardens and great gardens offer peaceful interludes on a touring day — a chance to stretch your legs, enjoy extraordinary horticulture, and recharge before the next section of road.

Scotland

  • Inverewe Garden, Wester Ross: An extraordinary subtropical garden on the NC500 route. Thanks to the Gulf Stream, exotic plants from around the world thrive on the northwest Highland coast. The contrast between the wild surroundings and the lush garden is remarkable.
  • Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh: 70 acres of stunning gardens with free entry. The glasshouses are world-class. Good motorcycle parking on Inverleith Row.
  • Crarae Garden, Argyll: A woodland garden on the shores of Loch Fyne. The A83 past here is excellent riding, and the garden is a peaceful lochside stop.

England

  • The Eden Project, Cornwall: The famous biomes housing tropical and Mediterranean plants. A unique stop on a Cornish tour. Good motorcycle parking and the surrounding roads are excellent.
  • RHS Harlow Carr, Harrogate: In the heart of Yorkshire riding country. The gardens are beautiful and Harrogate itself is a pleasant stop.
  • Alnwick Garden, Northumberland: A contemporary garden next to Alnwick Castle. The Poison Garden tour is fascinatingly dark. Excellent Northumberland riding nearby.
  • Bodnant Garden, Conwy Valley: Technically in Wales but accessible from England's Chester area. The laburnum arch in May/June is one of Britain's horticultural wonders.

Wales

  • National Botanic Garden of Wales, Carmarthenshire: The great glasshouse designed by Norman Foster houses Mediterranean plants. Set in rolling Welsh countryside with good riding roads in every direction.
  • Portmeirion, Gwynedd: Not strictly a garden but an Italianate village set in subtropical gardens on the Dwyryd Estuary. The ride along the coast to reach it passes through Snowdonia National Park.
Gardens are perfect mid-afternoon stops when concentration can wane. A 30-60 minute walk through beautiful surroundings refreshes your mind and body far better than another coffee at a petrol station. You'll ride better afterwards.

Planning Garden Stops

  • Most major gardens charge entry (£8-18) but National Trust and RHS members get free access to affiliated gardens
  • Spring (April-June) is peak flowering season for most gardens
  • Allow 1-2 hours for a satisfying visit
  • Most gardens have cafés serving good food — combine a garden stop with lunch
  • Check opening times — many close at 5pm or earlier

Great gardens are celebrations of beauty, patience, and craft. They offer a different kind of scenery from mountain passes — quieter, more intimate, and just as rewarding. faq.q: Do I have to pay to visit these gardens?
faq.a: Most major gardens charge entry, typically between £8 and £18. However, the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh has free entry to its grounds, and National Trust and RHS members get free access to affiliated gardens. If you already hold membership, plan your route around gardens in those schemes to keep costs down while still enjoying world-class horticulture.

faq.q: How long should I allow for a garden stop?
faq.a: Allow one to two hours for a satisfying visit. That is enough to walk the main areas, enjoy the glasshouses and take a break at the cafe. Gardens work best as a mid-afternoon interlude when concentration can wane; a 30 to 60 minute walk through beautiful surroundings refreshes mind and body far better than another petrol-station coffee, and you will ride better afterwards.

faq.q: When is the best time of year to visit?
faq.a: Spring, roughly April to June, is peak flowering season for most gardens. Bodnant Garden's famous laburnum arch peaks in May and June, and it is one of Britain's horticultural wonders. Check opening times before you go, as many gardens close at 5pm or earlier, and combine your visit with lunch since most have cafes serving good food.

faq.q: Can I combine a garden with good riding roads?
faq.a: Yes. Crarae Garden sits on Loch Fyne beside the excellent A83, Inverewe is directly on the NC500, and Alnwick Garden puts you in the heart of Northumberland's quiet coastal riding. The National Botanic Garden of Wales is surrounded by good roads in every direction, so a garden stop rarely means a detour away from the best tarmac.
